slots.instruction_en: Look at the picture and write its word from the box.
slots.prompt_rule: Six items, each one book object as picture: {kind:"object", name}. Put all six words, mixed, in "words" on the FIRST item only. Answer: the word. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Write the letters in ABC order.
slots.prompt_rule: Five items of three or four letters out of order, e.g. "d b c". Answer: the ordered letters.

slots.instruction_en: Join the letters to make a word.
slots.prompt_rule: Four items: a first letter and an ending (-at, -in, -an, -ig, -op) from the book, e.g. "c + at = ____". Answer: the word. Each item also carries picture: {kind:"object", name} of the answer word, in English for the artist; choose only words that can be drawn. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Put the letters in order to make a word.
slots.prompt_rule: Five three- or four-letter book words with letters mixed, e.g. "t a c". Only one word can be made. Answer: the word. Each item also carries picture: {kind:"object", name} of the answer word, in English for the artist; choose only words that can be drawn. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Look at the picture and fill in the missing letter.
slots.prompt_rule: Four items, each a book object as picture: {kind:"object", name} and its word with one letter blank, e.g. "b_g". Answer: the missing letter only, e.g. "a"; `accept` the full word. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

Four simple book words, e.g. "cat". Answer: one rhyming word; accept lists other real rhymes. Scheme: K 1 for a word that rhymes, K 1 for spelling it right. Each item also carries picture: {kind:"object", name} of the given word, in English for the artist; choose only words that can be drawn. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Write the name of each picture from the box.
slots.prompt_rule: Nine book objects (animals, fruit, school things), each as picture: {kind:"object", name}. Put all nine words, mixed, in "words" on the FIRST item only. Answer: the word. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: What is the child doing? Write the action word.
slots.prompt_rule: Five items, each a child doing one action from the book (run, jump, read, eat, sleep, swim) as picture: {kind:"scene", describe}. Answer: the -ing word the question asks for ("running"); the plain verb ("run") is also accepted and is never listed as an error. Each picture shows ONE action that has one clear word: never a child holding an object that could name the action (a book and a bag, a ball and a bat), and never an action another word fits (sit, rest and read on one picture). The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Fill in the blanks with words from the box.
slots.prompt_rule: Five short sentences from the book, each with one blank. Each sentence rules out every other word: only one word from the box fits each blank (never "likes to ___ in the park", where play, run or paint all fit). Put the five answer words, mixed, in "words" on the FIRST item. Scheme: K 1 for the right word. v35 (bd-5jmnfj.4.58.9): after writing each sentence, try every other box word in the blank and rewrite the sentence if a second word makes a sensible sentence ("The little bird can ___ sweet songs" fits sing and hear; "Dadi cannot ___ Pinky" fits hear and wash); a distractor never fits the grammar and the sense of the blank. No person's name in a Q9 sentence (use "we", "I", "the bird", "my mother"): the child has no context for a name. No sentence repeats a phrase of the oral listening story, which the child hears after this page.

slots.instruction_en: Circle the small letter that matches the capital letter.
slots.prompt_rule: Five items: a capital letter as the stem and four small letters as options (a, b, c, d). Never use I, l or L as a capital or as an option, since I and l look alike in print. Answer: the matching small letter.

Five book words with two letters missing, e.g. "m _ _ go"; the picture is the clue, so write no text clue. Answer: the missing letters only, e.g. "an"; `accept` the full word. Each item also carries picture: {kind:"object", name} of the answer word, in English for the artist; choose only words that can be drawn. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Look at the picture and write "This is a ____."
slots.prompt_rule: Five book objects as picture: {kind:"object", name}. Answer: "This is a <name>." Scheme: K 1 for naming the object, K 1 for spelling the word right; the frame "This is a ____." is printed, so no mark pays copying its capital letter or full stop. Each object's name begins with a consonant sound, so "a" is always right: never egg, apple, umbrella, orange, ant or ice cream. No object that any other question of this paper uses. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: What will they say? Write in the speech bubble.
slots.prompt_rule: Two greetings or polite words from the book (Good morning, Thank you, Sorry, Please), each a scene as picture: {kind:"scene", describe} of two children. The question names who speaks. The describe has no speech bubble and never mentions one, not even "next to the printed bubble" (the paper prints it) and shows exactly the thing the question names, in the same words, plain and never wrapped. The child who speaks stands on the right, next to the printed bubble, and the describe says "on the right". The question is about meeting, helping or saying sorry, never a gift or a present. Answer: the words. Scheme: K 2. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

slots.instruction_en: Rewrite the sentence with capital letters.
slots.prompt_rule: Four short sentences written all in small letters, each needing the capitals it names: the first letter, and a name or a day where the sentence has one (two capitals for "dani helps dadi."). Use names and days that no other question of this paper prints, and no word that Q6 answers or accepts. Answer: the corrected sentence. Scheme: one A point that names every capital the sentence needs.

slots.instruction_en: Choose is, am or are. Circle the answer.
slots.prompt_rule: Five short sentences with one blank; options exactly is, am, are. Answer: the right word.

lines_en: One mark per correct item unless the paper says otherwise.
Written marks only. Record the oral marks from the oral sheet, then add both on the class record.
